– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNestedJDOM` calls `doTest("nested", DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM, "foo;bar; baz ")`. Within `doTest`, the test fetches a JXPath context with an XML document loaded using the "JDOM" model. It then checks the value from the XPath `"test/text[@id='nested']"` against the expected string `"foo;bar; baz "` which includes a trailing space. The current bug report states that JXPath trims leading and trailing spaces from string values, which causes the test to fail since `"foo;bar; baz "` becomes `"foo;bar; baz"` during retrieval due to trimming.

From the code snippets we see:
- `doTest` initializes a JXPathContext on a document container created from "XmlSpace.xml" loaded with JDOM.
- The DocumentContainer constructor just stores the URL and model type.
- The test expects trailing spaces to be preserved in text node values.
- The `NodePointer.getValue()` method shows that the value is retrieved via a pointer and the default behavior ultimately returns `getNode()` value. We do not see any explicit trimming here.

The issue is consistent with the bug report: JXPath's internal processing of XML text nodes trims spaces, which is unexpected behavior. This is likely happening somewhere in JXPath's value retrieval mechanism or when converting XML text nodes to string values during XPath query evaluation with the JDOM model. The test expects preservation of whitespace exactly as in the XML source, but JXPath's handling trims them. This causes the test to fail when the assertion compares the retrieved string without trailing spaces, against the expected string with trailing spaces.

Since we see no trimming in `NodePointer.getValue()` itself, the trimming likely occurs deeper in the XML handling layer for the JDOM model, probably during conversion of the XML text node content to string or in XPath evaluation logic dealing with text nodes. The lack of prior bug reports or differences in other models suggests this trimming problem affects the JDOM model specifically.

Summary:
The bug is caused by JXPath automatically trimming leading/trailing spaces when retrieving XML text node string values in the JDOM model, which breaks expectations of preserving exact whitespace text content, leading the test case to fail.

Suggested locations to check:
- The code path that extracts text content from JDOM nodes and converts it to strings.
- XPath evaluation or Value retrieval methods specific to the JDOM model that may call `String.trim()` accidentally or use a method that discards whitespace.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
